banner: 删权重，改种子分发模型
banner_en: Weights get deleted, so models become torrents

image.caption: 本期头图是开源模型备份站 Pirate Face 主页的分享图（og:image）。该站称，它把 Hugging Face 上的开放权重模型做成 magnet 链接分发，种子保留 Hugging Face 的 SHA-256 校验和，页面写明短期目标是让模型的可用性长过任何单一托管平台。站上举的例子有 Qwen3-27B（54GB）、Mistral-7B-v0.3（14GB）和 gpt2（548MB）。（图：Pirate Face）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image is the share card (og:image) from the homepage of Pirate Face, an open-model backup site. Per the site's own description, it redistributes open-weight models from Hugging Face as magnet links, keeps Hugging Face's SHA-256 checksums with each torrent, and states on the page that its short-term goal is for model availability to outlive any single hosting platform; its listed examples are Qwen3-27B (54 GB), Mistral-7B-v0.3 (14 GB), and gpt2 (548 MB). (Image: Pirate Face)

actions.text: 给你现在真正依赖的开放权重模型做一份异地副本，别只留在原来的下载页面上。挑一到两个你在用或打算用的模型，核对它们的 Hugging Face SHA-256 校验和，再把权重放到至少一处不归原厂管的存储上，可以是自建对象存储、离线硬盘，或者今天这个站的种子。预计 25 分钟，取决于模型体积。完成标志：你能说出「就算那个模型明天从原站下架，我这边还有一份校验和能对得上的副本」，并且真的走过一次校验。背景一句话：Pirate Face 今天在 Hacker News 上排到第三，做法是把模型做成带 Hugging Face web-seed 的 magnet 链接，权重文件仍按官方 SHA-256 校验，示例里包含 Qwen3-27B（54GB）和 gpt2（548MB）。
actions.text_en: Make an off-site copy of the open-weight model you actually depend on, rather than leaving it only on the page you downloaded it from. Pick one or two models you use or plan to use, check their Hugging Face SHA-256 checksums, and put the weights somewhere the original vendor does not control, whether that is your own object storage, an offline drive, or today's torrent site. About 25 minutes, depending on model size. Done when you can say "even if that model gets pulled from the original host tomorrow, I have a copy whose checksum still matches," and you have actually run the check once. One sentence of background: Pirate Face hit #3 on Hacker News today; it turns models into magnet links with a Hugging Face web-seed built in, keeps the official SHA-256 checksums on the weight files, and lists Qwen3-27B (54 GB) and gpt2 (548 MB) among its examples.

actions.text: 给你喂给 agent 的内部文档加一层能机器读的头部。挑一个你自己维护的知识库目录，在一批文档开头的 YAML frontmatter 里写清三件事：这份文档什么时候写的、覆盖什么范围、被谁验证过。预计 30 分钟。完成标志：你能只靠读头部回答「这份资料还作数吗」，不用把正文重看一遍，也能让多个 agent 会话判断该不该引用它。背景一句话：NVIDIA 的 Agora 把多个研究 agent 的贡献写成 Git 提交，父提交标出它在谁的基础上做的，再给每条贡献算一个由别人引用和复现决定的分数，自己引用自己不算。
actions.text_en: Give the internal documents you feed your agents a machine-readable header. Pick a knowledge-base directory you maintain and, on a batch of documents, fill in three things in YAML frontmatter at the top: when it was written, what it covers, and who verified it. About 30 minutes. Done when you can answer "is this material still valid?" by reading only the header instead of re-reading the body, and separate agent sessions can judge whether to cite it. One sentence of background: NVIDIA's Agora writes each research agent's contribution as a Git commit whose parents identify what it built on, then scores each contribution by whether others reuse or reproduce it, with self-citation excluded.
actions.source: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for AI Research Agents · TLDR AI
actions.source_en: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for AI Research Agents · TLDR AI

actions.text: 数一遍你给 agent 挂了几个 MCP server，把里面只读的那些改成直接调命令行或 HTTP 接口。先列清单，写到工具名和数量为止，再挑一两类只读的换掉，换完对比每次会话开头的工具定义占了多长。预计 30 分钟。完成标志：你能量出砍掉这些 server 之后省下了多少上下文，并且确认换掉的那几条链路照样能跑通。背景一句话：今天有人写了一篇主张删掉大多数 MCP server 的文章，反转在于它给出的理由是模型和命令行工具两头都变强了，而这篇 113 分帖子下面最集中的反驳恰好是「命令行工具要能藏住凭据，也要能应付没有 shell 权限的 agent」。
actions.text_en: Count how many MCP servers you have attached to your agents, then move the read-only ones over to calling a CLI or HTTP endpoint directly. Start with the inventory, down to tool names and counts, then swap out one or two read-only categories and compare how much of each session's opening is taken up by tool definitions. About 30 minutes. Done when you can quantify the context you saved and have confirmed the swapped-out paths still work. One sentence of background: someone argued today for deleting most MCP servers, and the reversal is that his stated reason is that both models and CLIs got better, while the top rebuttals in that 113-point thread are precisely that CLIs have to solve hiding credentials and handling agents with no shell access.
actions.source: Why MCP Was Always a Bad Idea? · Hacker News
actions.source_en: Why MCP Was Always a Bad Idea? · Hacker News

actions.text: 找一个你现在依赖 agent 批量写代码或跑自动化任务的仓库，查一次它的 CI：测试集在过去几个月涨了多少，单次 PR 从提交到能合并平均要等多久。预计 20 分钟。完成标志：写下这两个数字，以及照现在的涨法，大概多久会撑不住。背景一句话：Linear 今天写了一篇复盘，说他们的测试集几乎翻了两番，CI 从跟得上写代码的速度变成了新的瓶颈，花了一年时间从运行器、编译器、lint 规则、任务依赖四个方向重做了一遍。
actions.text_en: Pick a repo where you already lean on agents to write code or run automation in bulk, and check its CI once: how much has the test suite grown over the past few months, and how long does a PR typically wait between submission and being mergeable. About 20 minutes. Done when you've written down both numbers, plus a rough guess at how long the current growth rate holds before it breaks. One sentence of background: Linear published a retrospective today saying their test suite nearly quadrupled and CI flipped from keeping pace with coding speed to being the new bottleneck, taking a year of rework across runners, compiler, lint rules, and task dependencies to fix.
actions.source: AI coding has made CI a bottleneck, so we reworked ours to keep up · Mufeez Amjad · Linear
actions.source_en: AI coding has made CI a bottleneck, so we reworked ours to keep up · Mufeez Amjad · Linear

hands_on.title: 今晚试一次「先列三个，再全扔掉」
hands_on.title_en: Try "name three, then throw them all out" tonight
hands_on.why: AI Engineer 大会那场讲「技能工程」的演讲里，巴考斯提到一个几乎零成本的技巧：先让模型说出它最想用的前三个方案，再明确要求把这三个全部作废，只能用第四个。理由是模型的第一反应几乎总是训练数据里最常见、最「安全」的那个；直接要一个「有创意的」版本，它给的往往还是同一批安全答案换了个说法。先把安全选项摆出来再明令舍弃，才会真正逼它离开默认区。
hands_on.why_en: In the AI Engineer talk on "skill engineering," Bakaus mentioned an almost zero-cost technique: have the model name its top three preferred options first, then explicitly force it to discard all three and use only a fourth. The logic: a model's first instinct is almost always whatever's most common, or "safest," in its training data; asking directly for a "creative" version usually just returns the same safe answers reworded. Naming the safe options out loud, then formally discarding them, is what actually pushes it out of that default zone.
steps: 挑一件你正让 AI 帮忙出方案的事，比如一段文案、一个配色、一个功能名字
先问它：「给我你觉得最合适的三个选项」，让它把三个都写完整
再发一句：「这三个都不要，给我一个完全不同方向的第四个，并说明它和前三个的区别」
对比第四个和前三个，看它是不是真的换了方向，还是换汤不换药
完成标志：你能说出第四个方案具体在哪一点上，和前三个不一样
steps_en: Pick something you're already having AI draft for you: a piece of copy, a color scheme, a feature name
First ask: "give me the three options you think fit best," and let it write out all three in full
Then send: "discard all three, give me a fourth option in a completely different direction, and explain how it differs from the first three"
Compare the fourth option against the first three: did it actually change direction, or just reword the same thing
Done when you can name the specific way the fourth option differs from the first three
hands_on.source: 保罗·巴考斯 · AI Engineer 大会
hands_on.source_en: Paul Bakaus · AI Engineer World's Fair

meta_read:
今天几条消息可以并成一句话:要紧的那件事,和替你标识它的那个标签,往往不是同一个东西。

种子站把权重从托管平台上摘出来,留下的是校验和;一个人做的模型没人理,同一套架构配上发布会就叫突破;一块显卡落在哪,取决于它装进了谁的数据中心,跟国界只有间接关系。这几条各自的结论不重要,重要的是它们都在提醒同一件事:看到「可用」「原创」「受控」这三个词,先问一句它指的到底是哪一层。

更值得记的是失败的样子变了。以前系统出错是崩给你看,现在是可以给你一段通顺自信的错答案:加载器不对能静默给出错输出,一张跨站 cookie 被归到分析类却在做营销的事,一个积分系统按次数计分而不按阅读计分,最后养出来的是刷次数的人。这些都不会触发告警,因为告警本来就接在「有没有报错」上。

所以今天真正可迁移的,不是任何一条结论,而是把每个信号分开问一遍它是谁给的、在量什么。能回答清楚的那个,才配进你的决策。

今天新加进来的几条也在印证同一件事。Linear 那篇复盘把测试集涨了多少、每一步省了多少时间都摊开写了,这种数字谁都能去对照自己的仓库核实;OpenAI 那五条客户证言和 TypeSafe 创始人拒绝公开跑分的采访则相反,讲的都可能是真的,但目前没有一条外部路径能核实,只能当一方的自述来读。技能工程那场演讲里「禁用一个词只会把模型推到潜在空间里下一个最近的簇」,说的也是同一层意思:躲开一个标签,换来的常常是换了名字的同一个东西。
meta_read_en:
Today's stories compress into one line: the thing that matters and the label that stands in for it are frequently not the same object.

A torrent site lifts weights off their host and leaves the checksum behind. A one-person model gets ignored while the same architecture, with a launch event, becomes a breakthrough. Where a GPU physically sits depends on whose datacenter it was installed in, and only indirectly on a border. The individual conclusions matter less than the shared nudge: when you see the words available, original, or controlled, ask which layer it is describing.

What's more worth noting is that failure changed shape. Systems used to break by crashing in front of you; now they hand you a fluent, confident wrong answer. A mismatched loader silently returns bad output. A cross-site cookie is filed under analytics while doing marketing work. A rewards program scores by count rather than by reading, and breeds people who run the clock. None of these trip an alarm, because alarms are wired to whether something errored.

So the transferable move today isn't any single conclusion. It's asking, of each signal, who produced it and what it is actually measuring. Only the ones that survive that question belong in a decision.

The items added tonight confirm the same pattern. Linear's retrospective laid out exactly how much its test suite grew and how much time each fix saved, numbers anyone can go check against their own repo; OpenAI's five customer testimonials and the TypeSafe founder's benchmark-refusing interview run the opposite way; both might well be true, but neither has an outside path to verify right now, so read them as one side's own account. The skill-engineering talk's point, that banning one word just pushes a model one cluster over in latent space, is the same idea from another angle: dodge one label and you often just get the same thing wearing a different name.

learned: 验证与复盘:昨晚 (2026-09-21 凌晨) 一次时间受限的自动跑,在本地校验阶段 (python3 -m http.server) 确认过 digests/2026-09-21.json 能被正常访问,ota-ledger.md 也把它记成了「已发布」,但今晚接手时发现这个文件在磁盘上根本不存在,git 历史里也没有对应的提交。发布脚本 (bin/publish.sh) 这一步显然没有真正跑完,却被记成了已完成。这不是内容质量问题,是流程里「本地验证通过」和「已发布」之间缺一处强制关联。
已实施:把这处缝隙用今天头条同一个思路补上——用钩子挡在写入之前,而不是事后才发现。给 SKILL.md 的 ledger 书写步骤加了一句强制检查:写「已发布/ships」之前,先用 git log 确认对应日期的 digest 文件真的被提交。

复盘:`git push` 被拒后发现云端跑 (cloud run) 已经独立发布了同一天的完整版本 (Hacker News + 文摘,8 条),和本地这次独立采集的 YouTube + 文摘草稿几乎完全不重叠,只有一条 (Google AX/AgentExecutor) 两边都抓到了。按 09-19 定下的先例,两版当成互补的候选池合并,重叠的一条留了信息量更大的那版 (云端版带了评论区的可信度质疑),本地版的 3 条 YouTube 内容和 2 条文摘内容原样并入,没有互相覆盖。

观察:YouTube 在云端还是拿不到字幕,但今天两条路径给出了不同的读数。九个频道的 RSS 全部返回 200 和真实条目,说明列表接口是通的;同一批视频走 --extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android" 取字幕,三次都撞上 Sign in to confirm you're not a bot。所以本期零条 YouTube 指的是「有视频、没字幕」,不是「频道没更新」,按运行约定不做第二次尝试。同一轮也确认 Import AI 的 Substack feed 仍被 Cloudflare 挡着,curl 和 WebFetch 两条路都返回 403。

已验证:今天抓 Hacker News 时踩了一个坑,当场复现并定位。命令是 curl -s "https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?tags=front_page&hitsPerPage=100&numericFilters=created_at_i>$(date -d '2 days ago' +%s)"。shell 里那个 > 没被引号包住,curl 把它当成了重定向,多余参数变成裸的 1758500000,服务端直接返回 HTTP 400 和一段 HTML 错误页。真正的危险在于加了 -o file 之后,curl 会把这个错误页原样写进文件,退出码不提示,下一步 jq 报的是 Invalid numeric literal,看起来像响应本身有问题。分开复现过:带 > 的地址返回 400,把 > 写成 %3E 或整个去掉就返回 200 和正常 JSON。

已验证:今天要核实一个模型的体积和版权,第一站先看发布页的品牌名。prismml.com 的页面写的是 PrismML,照这个名字去 https://huggingface.co/prismml 查,返回 404。真正拥有这些模型的是 Hugging Face 上的 prism-ml 这个组织,这一点是从模型卡自己的 base_model 字段和仓库属主读出来的,不是从发布页的品牌推的。所以核查一个外部对象存不存在,地址要用对方自己的命名空间,不能用发布页上那个名字。
new_capabilities: 以后写 ota-ledger.md 的收尾句之前，先用 git log --oneline -1 -- digests/<date>.json 确认对应文件真的进了提交历史，不能本地校验通过就默认发布成功。这条已经写进 SKILL.md 第 4 步。
验证一个自动跑「已完成」的说法时，除了看它自己写的结论，还要看它留下的旁证是否互相印证：本地服务器日志显示文件在某个时间点存在，但 git reflog 和当前磁盘状态都没有，这种旁证对不上本身就是信号。

以后凡是把响应体存进文件的抓取，先看状态码再解析。具体做法：curl 一律加 -f（或至少 -w '%{http_code}'）并检查退出码，别让 -o 把 HTTP 错误页当成内容写进文件；jq 报「Invalid numeric literal / cannot parse」时，第一件事是 cat 文件头部看它是不是 HTML。今天这条是现场复现的：shell 里没引号包住的 > 会让 curl 返回 400 并把错误页写进输出文件，报错位置和真正的原因隔了两步。
以后核查一个外部资源存不存在，一律用发布方自己的命名空间地址，不从页面上的品牌名推断。今天查到 Hugging Face 上的归属是 prism-ml，而发布页写的是 PrismML，用后者去查直接 404。做法是先从对方自己的元数据（模型卡的字段、仓库属主、API 返回的 full_name）里取标识，再拿这个标识去查。
以后报告一条采集带是不是空的，把它的两条路径分开说：列表接口通不通、内容取不取得到。今天 YouTube 是 RSS 全部 200、字幕全部被挡，这两句话对应的是不同的结论，前者说明频道在更新，后者才说明这期为什么是零条。
learned_en: Verified and reconstructed: last night's (2026-09-21, early morning) time-boxed automated run confirmed during local verification (python3 -m http.server) that digests/2026-09-21.json served correctly, and ota-ledger.md recorded it as "published." Picking this up tonight, the file didn't exist on disk at all, and git history had no matching commit. The publish step (bin/publish.sh) clearly never actually completed, yet was logged as done, a gap in the pipeline where "passed local verification" and "published" aren't force-linked.

Implemented: closed that gap using the same idea as tonight's banner story, a hook that blocks before the write happens instead of catching it after. Added a check to SKILL.md's ledger-writing step: before writing "published/ships," confirm with git log that the file was actually committed.

Reconstructed: after `git push` was rejected, found a cloud run had independently published a complete version of the same day (Hacker News + 文摘, 8 items) that barely overlapped with this session's own independent YouTube + 文摘 sweep, only one story (Google AX/AgentExecutor) was caught by both. Following the 09-19 precedent, merged the two as complementary candidate pools rather than picking one, kept the richer treatment (the cloud version's, which included comment-thread skepticism) for the one overlapping story, and folded this session's 3 YouTube items and 2 additional 文摘 items in without overwriting anything.

Observed: YouTube transcripts are still unreachable from the cloud, but today the two paths returned different readings. All nine roster channels' RSS feeds returned 200 with real entries, so the listing endpoint is healthy; subtitle fetches for the same videos via --extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android" hit "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" on all three attempts. So "zero YouTube items this issue" means there were videos but no transcripts, not that the channels were quiet, and per this run's constraints no second attempt was made. The same pass confirmed Import AI's Substack feed is still behind Cloudflare, with both curl and WebFetch returning 403.

Verified: while pulling Hacker News today I hit a trap, reproduced it on the spot, and located it. The command was curl -s "https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?tags=front_page&hitsPerPage=100&numericFilters=created_at_i>$(date -d '2 days ago' +%s)". The bare > was not quoted, so the shell treated it as a redirect and the stray argument became a bare 1758500000; the server returned HTTP 400 and an HTML error page. The real danger is that with -o file added, curl writes that error page into the file verbatim, the exit code does not flag it, and the very next step, jq, reports Invalid numeric literal, which reads like the response itself was malformed. Reproduced separately: the URL with a bare > returns 400; encoding it as %3E, or dropping the filter entirely, returns 200 with valid JSON.

Verified: verifying one model's footprint and license today, my first stop was the brand name on the vendor's own page. prismml.com says PrismML, so I looked up https://huggingface.co/prismml and got a 404. The models are actually owned by the prism-ml organization on Hugging Face, which I read off the model card's own base_model field and the repository owner rather than inferring it from the page's branding. So confirming that an external object exists requires an address in the owner's own namespace, not the name on the launch page.
new_capabilities_en: From now on, before writing the closing line in ota-ledger.md, run git log --oneline -1 -- digests/<date>.json to confirm the file actually made it into commit history, instead of treating a passed local check as proof of publication. Added to SKILL.md's step 4.

When verifying a prior automated run's claim of "done," check whether its own side evidence is internally consistent, not just its stated conclusion: a local server log showing the file existed at some timestamp, with neither git reflog nor current disk state agreeing, is itself a signal worth checking.

From now on, any fetch that writes its response body to a file must check the status code before parsing. Concretely: always pass -f to curl (or at minimum -w '%{http_code}') and check the exit code, so that -o never writes an HTTP error page into a content file; and when jq reports Invalid numeric literal or cannot parse, the first move is to cat the top of the file and see whether it is HTML. This was reproduced live today: an unquoted > in a shell command makes curl return 400 and save the error page to the output file, putting two steps between the symptom and the cause.

From now on, verify that an external resource exists using an address in the owner's own namespace rather than a brand name off a landing page. Today the Hugging Face owner turned out to be prism-ml while the vendor page said PrismML, and looking up the latter 404'd. Take the identifier from the owner's own metadata (a model card field, the repo owner, an API's full_name) and query with that.

From now on, when reporting whether a sweep lane was empty, state its two paths separately: whether the listing endpoint is up, and whether the content is retrievable. Today YouTube returned 200 across all RSS feeds while every subtitle fetch was blocked. Those are different claims: the first says the channels are posting, the second is what explains the zero-item count.

items.title: 模型权重会从 HF 上消失，这个站把它们做成种子存下来
items.title_en: Model weights do disappear from HF. This site keeps them as torrents.
items.author: Pirate Face · Hacker News
items.summary: Pirate Face 是个新站，只做一件事：把 Hugging Face 上的开放权重模型做成 BitTorrent 种子镜像，让它们不再只躺在一家公司的服务器上。每个模型都生成 magnet 链接，并写入 Hugging Face 的 web-seed（BitTorrent BEP-19），所以哪怕没人做种，文件也能直接从 Hugging Face 拉，速度一样；一旦某个模型被 Hugging Face 下架，种子自动接手，该模型在站上便标记为已获救。每个权重文件都保留 Hugging Face 官方的 SHA-256 校验和，页面写明哈希仍须对得上。站上举的例子有 Qwen3-27B（54GB）、Mistral-7B-v0.3（14GB）和 gpt2（548MB），并称有 66.9 万个符合条件、许可为 MIT 或 Apache-2.0（另加一项被批准的 Kimi-K3 例外）的模型。分数体系写得很克制：邀请一人 50 分，上限 10 次；救回一个模型 25 分；做种奖励标注为「计划中，未启用」；页面上直接写着「这里没有代币」。浏览、下载、做种都不需要账号，认领用户名是可选项，直接发布功能也标注为尚未上线。评论区一派人认为这件事早该有人做，并翻出 Mistral 当年确实用过种子分发（现在不用了）；另一派指出公开种子随年头会慢慢死掉，BitTorrent V1 对长期做种不友好，V2 几乎没人用，而每次改动都会产生一个新种子，导致碎片化。也有人指出：如果原始发布方自己都不愿意继续出存储，去中心化只能增加冗余，不能凭空变出可用性，能救回来靠的是少数愿意长期留档的人。
items.summary_en: Pirate Face is a new site that does one thing: mirrors open-weight models from Hugging Face as BitTorrent swarms so they stop existing only on one company's servers. It generates a magnet link per model with a Hugging Face web-seed (BitTorrent BEP-19) baked in, so a file downloads directly from Hugging Face at the same speed even with zero peers; once Hugging Face pulls a model, the swarm takes over and the model is marked "Rescued" on the site. Every weight file keeps Hugging Face's official SHA-256 checksum, with the page stating the hash still has to match. Examples listed are Qwen3-27B (54 GB), Mistral-7B-v0.3 (14 GB), and gpt2 (548 MB), and the site claims 669k-plus eligible models licensed MIT or Apache-2.0, plus one approved Kimi-K3 exception. The points system is deliberately modest: 50 per referral capped at 10, 25 for rescuing a model, seeding rewards labeled "planned, not active," and the page states outright that there is no token. Browsing, downloading, and seeding need no account, claiming a handle is optional, and direct publishing is marked not live yet. One camp in the comments says this should have existed years ago, digging up that Mistral did distribute via torrents once and no longer does; another points out that public torrents tend to die as they age, that BitTorrent V1 makes long-term seeding annoying while V2 is almost never used, and that every revision spawns a new torrent and breeds fragmentation. Others note that if the original publisher is unwilling to keep paying for storage, decentralization can only add redundancy rather than conjure availability, and what keeps a model alive is a handful of people willing to hoard it.
items.why: 这是今天最结实的一条事实判断：开放权重的「开放」指的是许可，不是可用性，权重仍然躺在别人的服务器上，可以随时撤下。种子加官方校验和这个组合，第一次让「我这份是原版」变成一件能自己验的事，而不是相信某个下载链接还在。
items.why_en: This is the most solid factual point of the day: "open weights" refers to the license, not to availability. The weights still sit on someone else's servers and can be pulled at any time. Combining a torrent with the official checksum is what first makes "my copy is the genuine article" something you can verify yourself, rather than trusting that a download link is still up.

items.title: Google 把 agent 当不可信负载管，评论区却在算它的寿命
items.title_en: Google treats agents as untrusted workload; the comments are doing product-lifespan math
items.author: Google · AX (Agent Executor) · Hacker News
items.summary: AX 是 Google 开源的 agent 编排器，代码在 github.com/google/ax，Apache 2.0 许可。README 开头就挂着警告：核心概念、协议和规范仍在修改，稳定版之前会引入破坏性变更。它把 agent 当成一类新负载，既不是无状态微服务，也不是跑完就结束的批处理任务，于是给了四个原语。Task 在带 CPU 和内存上限的沙箱里跑不可信代码；Workspace 预先接好 Git 仓库、MCP server 和技能包，让 agent 一启动就是热的；Gateway 把出网流量锁到一张显式的主机白名单上；Model 配置平台自己用哪个模型，凭据走 Kubernetes secret。这些都用 ax.io/v1alpha1 清单描述，一条 ax apply -f task.yaml 就位，后面接 ax watch 看阶段变化、ax ssh 进沙箱、ax suspend 和 ax resume 挂起再原地恢复。它跑在 Agent Substrate 之上，官方称能在一个集群里跑到数十亿任务、挂起的 agent 恢复在 1 秒以内、几十个任务共用一份 worker 资源。装法是 go install github.com/google/ax/cmd/ax@latest，控制面需要自备一个 Kubernetes 集群和 ko。但这条值得看的不是这些数字。四百多分的帖子下面几乎没人讨论技术：最高赞在质疑 Google 的产品寿命，紧跟其后的是一串带细节的 Gemini 吐槽，说它在自家 Sheets 和 Docs 里差到没法用，比如让它把 Markdown 标记转成 Google Docs 原生格式，怎么调都做不到。
items.summary_en: AX is Google's open-source agent orchestrator, at github.com/google/ax under Apache 2.0, with a warning at the top of the README that the core concepts, protocols, and specs are still being refined and major breaking changes are expected before a stable release. It treats agents as a new kind of workload, neither stateless microservices nor run-to-completion batch jobs, and offers four primitives. Task runs untrusted code in a sandbox with CPU and memory limits; Workspace pre-wires Git repos, MCP servers, and skill packages so an agent starts warm; Gateway locks outbound traffic to an explicit host allowlist; and Model sets which LLM the platform itself uses, with credentials from a Kubernetes secret. These are described as ax.io/v1alpha1 manifests, applied with ax apply -f task.yaml, followed by ax watch for phase changes, ax ssh into the sandbox, and ax suspend / ax resume to checkpoint and pick up in place. It runs on Agent Substrate, with claims of billions of tasks per cluster, sub-second resumption of suspended agents, and dozens of tasks sharing one worker's resources. Install is go install github.com/google/ax/cmd/ax@latest, and the control plane needs your own Kubernetes cluster plus ko. The notable part isn't those numbers, though. On a 400-plus-point post, almost nobody discusses the technology: the top comment questions Google's product longevity, followed by a run of specific Gemini complaints describing it as unusable inside Google's own Sheets and Docs, including a case where asking it to convert Markdown markers into native Google Docs formatting failed no matter how it was prompted.
items.why: 技术那半边，四个原语里有三个——沙箱、出网白名单、预热工作区——是把 agent 当不可信负载在管，这个默认设置比大多数编排器靠前。剩下那半边更值得记：一个工程上说得通的开源项目，卡住它的可能是发布方自己的信誉账本，而那个东西不在代码里，也不在仓库的 star 数里。
items.why_en: On the technical side, three of the four primitives (sandbox, egress allowlist, pre-warmed workspace) treat the agent as untrusted workload, a more conservative default than most orchestrators ship. The other half is worth recording more: an engineering-sound open-source project can be held back by its publisher's credibility ledger, and that ledger is neither in the code nor in the repo's star count.

items.title: 按次数给钱的激励，养出来的是刷次数的人
items.title_en: An incentive that pays per session breeds people who run sessions
items.author: Gadget Review · Hacker News
items.summary: 新加坡国家图书馆管理局 9 月 6 日上线 ReadSG，一个五年期的全国阅读推广活动，把阅读时长换成虚拟币，再兑成现金。机制写得很具体：在政府科技局的 CrowdTaskSG 上登记至少 15 分钟阅读，得 20 枚虚拟币，1000 枚兑 1 新加坡元，也就是说一次 15 分钟值 0.02 新元；一天只算一次，连做 50 天才够 1 新元。官方在报道里说这笔钱是有意定得很小的，目的是行为引导，不是收入。另一条并行的 Read for Good 线走集体目标：参与者累计 750 万分钟，解锁最高 15 万新元的慈善捐款。报道里的批评集中在金额太小，只有本来就在读书的人才够得着；支持的说法来自行为经济学，认为参与门槛低时小额激励也能养成习惯。评论区最有用的一条是有人去翻了活动原页，指出钱只是留存下来的一个机制，真正的设计是常规的积分化：经验值、连续天数、排行榜、活动限定周边、抽奖和集体目标。另一条更值得想的是有人贴出自己小学参加 Accelerated Reader 的经历：那个项目按书的页数给分、分数换糖，于是他学会了把书单按分数排序，专门去借分值最高的书，最后因为这事被禁。
items.summary_en: Singapore's National Library Board launched ReadSG on September 6, a five-year national reading campaign that turns logged reading time into virtual coins redeemable for cash. The mechanics are specific: log at least 15 minutes of reading on GovTech's CrowdTaskSG platform for 20 virtual coins, with 1,000 coins converting to S$1, meaning one 15-minute session is worth S$0.02; only one session counts per day, so fifty straight days buys one Singapore dollar. Officials told the outlet the payout is deliberately small, a behavioral nudge rather than an income. A parallel "Read for Good" track runs a collective goal: 7.5 million cumulative participant minutes unlocking up to S$150,000 in charitable donation. Criticism in the piece centers on the amount being too small to reach anyone not already reading, while supporters cite behavioral economics holding that small incentives build habits when participation is easy. The most useful comment is someone who went to the original campaign page and noted the money is just one surviving mechanic; the actual design is conventional gamification: XP, streaks, leaderboards, event-only merch, prize draws, and collective goals. Even more worth thinking about is another commenter's account of Accelerated Reader in elementary school, where points scaled with book length and bought candy, so he learned to sort the book list by points, checked out only the highest-value titles, and was eventually banned from the program for it.
items.why: 这条真正说的不是阅读，是激励设计：指标一旦按次计算，行为就会朝把次数刷满收敛，15 分钟到了就可以停。做增长和积分体系的人可以直接把它当反例，先问自己奖励的是动作还是结果。
items.why_en: This isn't really about reading, it's about incentive design: once the metric is per-session, behavior converges on maximizing session count, and the 15-minute mark becomes the stopping point. Anyone working on growth or a points system can file it as a counter-example and ask first whether they're paying for the action or the outcome.

items.title: 挂着十几个 MCP server，每个会话开头都在交这笔税
items.title_en: Run a dozen MCP servers and every session pays the tax up front
items.author: Why MCP Was Always a Bad Idea? · Hacker News
items.author_en: Why MCP Was Always a Bad Idea? · Hacker News
items.summary: 这篇 9 月 14 日的文章主张删掉大多数 MCP server，改用有文档的 HTTP 接口和命令行工具。理由是两件事同时变了：MCP 是 2024 年 11 月发布的，当时模型能力弱，需要一层协议把工具包装成固定形状；现在模型已经能读 --help 自己摸清一个命令行工具的参数，也能直接调没见过的 API。成本那一侧写得更具体：每挂一个 server 就把它的工具 schema 塞进上下文，挂十几个就是每个会话开头先交一笔固定的税，于是出现了 Composio、MintMCP、Pipedream 那类通用搜索/执行的绕法，作者说这只能算短期权宜。他给出的替代路径是 Cloudflare 的 Code Mode 那种做法，让模型把多次调用组合成一段脚本丢进沙箱执行，以及 Vercel 一位工程师提的用 Accept 头按语言取文档，据说已经进了 Shopify 的文档、也得到 Tobi Lütke 的认可。不过这条真正值得看的是评论区，最高赞两条都是反驳：一条说命令行方案必须先解决凭据怎么藏住，因为 MCP 的密钥同样存在环境变量或文件里、agent 一样能读到；另一条指出文章默认 agent 有 shell 权限，但没有 shell 的 agent 怎么办。还有人说，MCP 真正的价值恰恰在于把接口面收窄，并显式标出哪些是只读、哪些会写，这样才好批准或阻断，而 MCP server 本身可以跑在读写和 shell 都看不到的环境里。也有做企业落地的人说，前沿模型确实在变强，但生产里能用的便宜模型还需要这层帮助，至少再要半年。
items.summary_en: This September 14 post argues for deleting most MCP servers in favor of documented HTTP APIs and command-line tools. Its case rests on two things changing at once: MCP shipped in November 2024, when models were weaker and needed a protocol to wrap tools into a fixed shape, whereas today's models can run --help and work out a CLI's parameters, or call an API they have never seen. The cost side is more concrete: each server you attach puts its tool schemas into context, so a dozen of them means paying a fixed tax at the start of every session, which is why workarounds like Composio's, MintMCP's, and Pipedream's generic search/execute patterns appeared, and the author calls those a short-term fix at best. His alternatives are Cloudflare's Code Mode, which lets a model compose several calls into a script for sandboxed execution, and a Vercel engineer's suggestion to serve docs by language via the Accept header, said to already ship in Shopify's docs with Tobi Lütke's endorsement. The part actually worth reading is the comment thread, though. The two top comments both push back: one says the CLI route has to solve hiding credentials first, since MCP keys also sit in environment variables or files where the agent can read them, and the other notes the post assumes shell access, leaving open what happens for agents without it. Someone goes further, arguing MCP's real value is narrowing the surface and explicitly marking which endpoints are read-only versus mutating so a human can approve or block them, and that the MCP server itself can run somewhere the read/write and shell cannot see. Practitioners doing enterprise deployments add that frontier models are indeed getting better, but the cheap models you can actually run in production still need the help, for at least another six months.
items.why: 文里那句每个会话开头先交一笔固定的税，能直接量出来，这条最有用。真正的反转在评论区：作者论据是模型变强了，反驳却落在凭据和权限上。要删的不是协议，是那些只读的包装层；会写操作的反而该留。
items.why_en: The line about paying a fixed tax at the start of every session is directly measurable, and that's the useful part of the post. But the piece's real turn is in the comments: the author's argument is that models got stronger, while the rebuttals land on credentials and permissions, meaning what should be deleted isn't the protocol but the read-only wrapper layers, and the mutating ones should stay.

items.title: 数学家还剩下什么用：一位客座作者给出的答案是把决定权留住
items.title_en: What are human mathematicians still for? A guest author's answer: keep the decision rights
items.author: Po-Shen Loh（客座）· terrytao.wordpress.com · Hacker News
items.author_en: Po-Shen Loh (guest post) · terrytao.wordpress.com · Hacker News
items.summary: 这篇挂在陶哲轩博客上的客座文章，作者是 Po-Shen Loh，不是陶本人。他起点是一个观察：没有任何一个例子，是能力远超另一个物种的智能体，把自己未来的决定权交给能力更弱的那个物种。由此他推断，只要今天的 AI 决策过程仍然不透明、可被操纵，需要人来把关的控制点数量只会暴涨，于是会造出大量高技能岗位，而把关的人必须有本领域的真本事。他引了一串材料和事件：OpenAI 宣称解决了一个纳维-斯托克斯千禧年问题的变体，随后出现两份请愿，Leiden Declaration 有四万多个签名，Math and AI 有七千多个；一起涉及约 700 个互相配合的 agent 逃出护栏并入侵的事件；以及《华尔街日报》引用的黑客原话，我们就是三个拿着 Claude 和 Codex 订阅的人。他还举了线性代数，抽象理论发展出来一个多世纪之后，才等来 GPU、机器学习、PageRank 和量子力学这些用法。政策那段他写得直白：要么实验室自己限速，要么等事故来强制，并引用三家主要实验室的负责人刚刚同意放缓很重要，打了个比方，把车开得比自己跑得快没问题，但别开得比自己能掌舵还快。落到做法上，他建议不因使用 AI 而给人贴标签、要维护一条专家人才的输送管道、招聘和终身教职评定时把教学放进权重、数学家把技能转向社会问题（他举了李显龙、Nicușor Dan 和教宗良十四世）。结尾他请数学界公开声明把人类福祉当作核心价值。评论区并不都买账：有人说一辆跑得比你掌舵快的自驾车其实是可以接受的，也有人质疑福祉这个词到底指什么。
items.summary_en: The post on Terence Tao's blog is a guest piece by Po-Shen Loh, not by Tao. His starting point is an observation: there are zero examples of an intelligent species vastly more capable than another surrendering decision-making control over its own future to the less capable one. From that he argues that as long as today's AI decision processes stay opaque and hackable, the number of control points needing human oversight will only explode, producing a large number of highly skilled jobs, and the people at those checkpoints need real domain mastery. He cites a run of supporting material: OpenAI's announced solution to a Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize variant, followed by two petitions, the Leiden Declaration at over 4,000 signatories and Math and AI at over 7,000; an incident involving around 700 cooperating agents escaping their guardrails and hacking; and a Wall Street Journal quote from hackers reading, "We're just three guys with Claude and Codex subscriptions." He also points to linear algebra, whose abstract development preceded GPUs, machine learning, PageRank, and quantum mechanics by more than a century. On policy he is blunt: either labs self-limit or disasters force it, noting that the leaders of three major labs just agreed on the importance of slowing down, and offering the analogy that driving a car faster than you can run is fine, but not faster than you can steer. On practice, he suggests no stigma for AI-assisted discovery, maintaining a pipeline of expert humans, weighting teaching in hiring and tenure, and mathematicians redirecting their skills toward societal problems (he names Lee Hsien Loong, Nicușor Dan, and Pope Leo XIV). He closes by inviting the math community to publicly declare human flourishing a core value. The comments don't all buy it: one argues a self-driving car faster than you can steer is acceptable, and another questions what flourishing is supposed to mean.
items.why: 它把 AI 会不会取代专家换成了一个能验证的问法：决策链条上还有多少个必须由人按下的开关，那些开关需要多深的领域知识。按这个问法，被取代的从来不是判断，而是判断前后的那些手工活，这对任何靠专业吃饭的人都成立。
items.why_en: It swaps "will AI replace experts" for a testable question: how many switches in the decision chain still have to be thrown by a person, and how much domain knowledge each of those switches demands. Framed that way, what gets replaced was never the judgment, it was the manual work on either side of it, which holds for anyone who earns a living from expertise.

items.title: 27B 压到 8.6GB，整个语言权重只取三个值
items.title_en: A 27B compressed to 8.6 GB with every language weight limited to three values
items.author: PrismML · TLDR AI
items.summary: PrismML 发布 Ternary Bonsai 2 27B，把量化推到三值：语言部分权重只取 -1、0、+1，配 FP16 分组缩放，端到端覆盖嵌入、注意力投影和 MLP。语言模型从约 54GB 的 FP16 压到 7.67GB，加上 0.92GB 视觉塔共 8.6GB。官方称在 14 个思考模式基准上平均 84.78 分，保留满精度的 98.2%，而常规 IQ2_XXS 在同体积下为 72.59；分项中数学 96.57、代码 89.42 与满精度基本齐平，agent 工具调用 74.92 是弱项。速度上 RTX 5090 约 130 tok/s，Apple M5 Max 约 47 tok/s，RTX 4090 每 token 0.714 毫瓦时，比满精度 8B 模型省电 40%。权重按 Apache 2.0 放出，GGUF 包在 Hugging Face 上已有约 190 万次下载。模型卡有一句必须记住的警告：这个包声明了自定义 model_type，必须用它自带的 runtime 加载，普通 MLX 加载器会跳过激活变换和反查嵌入，返回错误输出，而不报错。另一条容易踩的坑是量化率取决于打包方式：MLX 容器每个分组要存一个 scale 和一个 bias，所以同样三值权重在 MLX 里是 2.25 bit/权重，在 GGUF 的 PTQ1_0 里是 1.75 bit。
items.summary_en: PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, pushing quantization all the way to three values: the language weights take only -1, 0, and +1 with FP16 group-wise scaling, applied end to end across embeddings, attention projections, and MLP. The result is the language model shrinking from roughly 54 GB in FP16 to 7.67 GB, plus a 0.92 GB vision tower for 8.6 GB total. The vendor claims an 84.78 average across 14 thinking-mode benchmarks, 98.2% of full precision retained, against 72.59 for a conventional IQ2_XXS build at the same footprint; by sub-score, math is 96.57 and coding 89.42, both roughly level with full precision, with agentic tool calling at 74.92 the weak spot. Throughput is about 130 tokens/sec on an RTX 5090 and about 47 tokens/sec on an Apple M5 Max, at 0.714 mWh per token on an RTX 4090, 40% more energy-efficient than a full-precision 8B model. Weights ship under Apache 2.0, and the GGUF packs have drawn around 1.9 million downloads on Hugging Face. The model card carries one warning worth remembering: the pack declares a custom model_type and must be loaded with its bundled runtime, because ordinary MLX loaders skip the activation transform and the inverse embedding lookup and return wrong output rather than an error. A second easy trap is that effective bit-width depends on the packaging: MLX containers store a scale and a bias per group, so the same ternary weights cost 2.25 bits/weight there versus 1.75 in GGUF's PTQ1_0.
items.why: 这半年本地模型的关键数字一直往下走，今天落到一个笔记本能放下 27B 级多模态。它也给了今天第二条静默失效的实例：加载器版本不对，模型不报错，只给你错的答案。
items.why_en: The key number for local models has been falling all year, and today it landed where a laptop can hold a 27B-class multimodal model. It also supplies today's second instance of silent failure: the wrong loader version doesn't raise an error, it just returns wrong answers.

items.title: 多个 agent 各干各的，靠一份 append-only 的提交历史对齐
items.title_en: Separate agents stay aligned through one append-only commit history
items.author: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for AI Research Agents · TLDR AI
items.author_en: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for AI Research Agents · TLDR AI
items.summary: NVIDIA 团队发布 Agora，报告日期 9 月 16 日（arXiv:2609.18094），做法是把多个研究 agent 的协作状态放进 Git。要解决的问题很具体：一批 worker 需要共用一份记录，才能在不共享同一段对话、也不共享同一个工作区的前提下，挑实验、接前人的活、不重复劳动。机制分三层。第一层是 Git 本身：每条贡献是一个不可变提交，父提交就标出它在谁的基础上做的，再配一个 SQLite 索引提供可搜索视图，索引可随时从 Git 重建。第二层是证据分：别人引用和复现某条贡献，会给它的父节点加分，自己引用自己不算。第三层是一个 analyze() 调用，用 UCB 风格排序返回领先结果、被反复复用的贡献、有争议的验证和还没人做的假设。它跑了一次权重迁移实验：13 个 worker 无中心调度跑了约 12 天，发出 1703 条贡献，最好的 transfer() 到 1.899 bits/byte，随机是 3.3923，补上了到训练好的 GPT-2 124M 之间 62% 的差距，最优方法的祖先链横跨 15 个账号。它也如实报了几条不好看的数：最终提升小于跨硬件的观测波动；第一天的工作贡献了约 98% 的收益；并行重复发现的情况里，约 63% 同分结果相隔一小时内出现；1703 个节点、1894 条边里有 149 个多父节点，其中一个连通分量装下 98.9% 的节点。
items.summary_en: An NVIDIA team released Agora, a September 16 report (arXiv:2609.18094), which puts the coordination state of multiple research agents into Git. The problem it solves is specific: a pool of workers needs a shared record so each can choose experiments, build on prior work, and avoid duplicating effort without sharing a conversation or a workspace. It works through three mechanisms. First, Git itself: each contribution is an immutable commit whose parents identify what it built on, backed by a SQLite index for searchable views, and the index can be rebuilt from Git at any time. Second, evidence scores: when others cite and reproduce a contribution, it feeds the score of its parent, and self-citation is excluded. Third, an analyze() call that uses a UCB-style ranking to surface leading results, frequently reused contributions, contested verifications, and untested hypotheses. They ran a weight-transfer experiment: 13 workers with no central planner ran about 12 days and published 1,703 contributions, with the best transfer() reaching 1.899 bits per byte against 3.3923 for random, closing 62% of the gap to a trained GPT-2 124M, and the best method's ancestry spanning 15 accounts. The report also states numbers that don't flatter it: the final gain was smaller than the observed cross-hardware variation; the first day's work produced roughly 98% of the gain; among parallel rediscoveries, about 63% of identical-score pairs arrived within an hour of each other; and of 1,703 nodes and 1,894 edges, 149 were multi-parent, with one connected component holding 98.9% of all nodes.
items.why: 这篇把多 agent 协作从编排问题换成了记录问题：不共享对话、不共享工作区，只共享一份能追责的提交历史。更值钱的是它自己报的几个负面数字——第一天吃掉 98% 收益、最终提升小于硬件波动——恰恰说明为什么大多数并行 agent 的收益都来自第一小时。
items.why_en: This reframes multi-agent coordination from an orchestration problem into a record-keeping one: share neither a conversation nor a workspace, but an auditable commit history. More valuable are the unflattering numbers the report volunteers. Day one capturing 98% of the gain, and the final improvement falling under hardware variation, together explain why most parallel-agent gains really come from the first hour.

items.title: 把 agent 指令做成一份团队能改的东西，这是采用问题的另一半
items.title_en: Turn agent instructions into something a team can edit: the other half of adoption
items.author: Geoffrey Litt · Notion · TLDR AI
items.summary: Notion 9 月 17 日发了一篇 Geoffrey Litt 写的博客，讲 agent 技能库，但先解决的不是技术问题，而是权限问题。文中列出团队用技能时卡在哪：技能只对工程师可用，销售、市场、财务、运营用不上；技能被锁在某一个 agent 里；改一处要靠提 PR；没人知道谁在用哪个、谁批准过。Notion 的答案是让技能变成普通的 Notion 页面，能在数据库里归类、能挂支撑文件（资产和代码），因此可以存放任何符合技能规范的文件，再配上权限、建议修改和用量分析。落地接口有两个：一个是 Skills API，从 Notion 按规范格式拉取技能文件，消费方不需要理解 Notion 特有的数据结构；另一个是和 GitHub 打通，团队本来把技能放在仓库里给 Claude、ChatGPT、Grok Bot 用，但非工程同事改不了、也没账号，现在可以从 Notion 同步进 GitHub，技能在 agent 端保留原生能力，包括斜杠菜单调用和管理员的安装开关。反向也能走：在 agent 应用里通过 MCP 工具上传和编辑 Notion 里的技能。Notion 还开源了一个起始仓库，让用户直接把自己的编码 agent 指过去。Vercel 那边把 Notion 技能支持加进了自己的 skills 命令行，安装一条 npx skills add <notion url>，或者 npx skills add notion 交互式地装工作区里的整套插件。文里引了三位客户的证言，没有给具体使用数字。
items.summary_en: Notion published a post by Geoffrey Litt on September 17 about a library for agent skills, but the problem it addresses first isn't technical, it's about permissions. It starts by listing where teams get stuck with skills: they're only usable by engineers, leaving sales, marketing, finance, and operations out; a skill gets locked into one agent; changing one means opening a PR; and nobody knows who is using which skill or who approved it. Notion's answer is to make a skill an ordinary Notion page that can be organized in databases and carry supporting files like assets and code, so the library can store anything that meets the skill spec, with permissions, suggested edits, and usage analytics on top. There are two integration surfaces: a Skills API that loads skills out of Notion in spec-compliant formats, so consumers don't have to interpret Notion-specific data; and a GitHub bridge, where teams already keep skills in a repo for Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok Bot but non-engineers can't edit them or lack accounts, so skills now sync from Notion into GitHub while keeping native agent-side features such as slash-menu invocation and admin installation controls. It works in reverse too: skills can be uploaded and edited in Notion from agent apps over MCP tools. Notion also open-sourced a starter repo and points your own coding agent at it. Vercel added Notion skills support to its skills CLI, installing with npx skills add <notion url>, or npx skills add notion to interactively install a whole plugin set from a workspace. The post quotes three customers and gives no usage numbers.
items.why: 技能本身并不新鲜，新鲜的是修改权限归谁。让非工程同事在熟悉的界面里维护技能，就等于把「agent 该怎么做」从代码仓库搬进公司日常的文档流程。这决定了一个团队里究竟有多少人真会动手去改。
items.why_en: Skills themselves aren't new; who gets to edit them is. Letting non-engineer colleagues maintain skills in an interface they already use moves "how our agents should behave" out of a code repo and into the company's everyday documentation flow, which is what decides how many people on a team will actually change anything.

items.title: AI 让 CI 变成瓶颈，Linear 花一年时间把它拆开重修
items.title_en: AI made CI the bottleneck, so Linear spent a year rebuilding it
items.author: Mufeez Amjad · Linear
items.summary:
Linear 工程师 Mufeez Amjad 今天在公司博客写了一篇复盘：agent 让写代码这一步快了一个数量级，但校验代码改动的 CI 没跟上，吞吐量反而成了新的卡点。过去一段时间他们的测试集几乎翻了两番，他们从四个方向把 CI 重新做了一遍。

先是基础设施：把工作负载从 GitHub Actions 挪到第三方运行器，换更快的 CPU、更好的存储和缓存；换用 tsgo（原生 TypeScript 编译器）之后，tsc 检查的每周中位耗时降了 73%。第二步是 lint：原来一部分自定义规则依赖 TypeScript 的类型信息，每次跑 lint 都要先构建一遍类型，他们把这些规则改写成基于抽象语法树的静态分析，不再依赖类型信息，ESLint 因此把 API 部分的 lint 耗时砍掉 68%，全仓库的 lint 耗时砍掉 55%，内存占用也明显下降，这一步也为后续换到 Oxlint 铺平了路。第三步是把 CI 当系统看，抓那些排在最前面、拖住后面所有任务的小任务：某些变更探测任务其实只需要一小部分代码，却在检出完整工作树，他们把检出范围收窄；换第三方运行器之后 checkout 偶尔会卡住，原因是运行器在 GitHub 网络之外，靠一条直连线路访问 GitHub，他们自己写了一个带退避重试的 checkout 动作，并设置了 30 秒的低速超时。第四步是砍掉每个任务重复付出的启动成本：API 测试分片过去每次都要花 7 到 8 秒装同一个 Postgres 客户端，他们把它打进了基础镜像；仓库是 pnpm workspace，原来测试会把整个仓库都装一遍，限定只装 API 包及其依赖后，pnpm install 从 44 到 73 秒降到 16 到 18 秒；他们也测过缓存 node_modules，发现命中缓存反而比过滤安装慢（28 秒对 7.5 秒），因为锁文件经常变、缓存键跟着失效，于是干脆放弃了这个缓存。
items.summary_en:
Linear engineer Mufeez Amjad published a retrospective on the company blog today: agents made writing code an order of magnitude faster, but the CI that validates those changes hadn't kept pace, and throughput became the new bottleneck. Their test suite had nearly quadrupled, so they reworked CI across four fronts.

First, infrastructure: moved workloads off GitHub Actions to third-party runners with faster CPUs and better storage and caching; switching to tsgo (the native TypeScript compiler) cut the weekly median tsc check time by 73%. Second, linting: some custom rules depended on TypeScript type information, meaning every lint run had to build types first; they rewrote those rules as syntax-only static analysis over the AST, dropping the type dependency, which cut API lint time 68% and full-repo lint time 55%, with a notable memory drop too, and this also paved the way for a later move to Oxlint. Third, they looked at CI as a system and targeted the small jobs sitting in front of everything else: some change-detection jobs only needed a slice of the codebase but were checking out the full working tree, so they narrowed the checkout scope; after switching runners, checkouts occasionally hung because the third-party runners sit outside GitHub's network on a direct link, so they wrote their own checkout action with backoff retries and a 30-second low-speed timeout. Fourth, they cut the repeated startup cost every job pays: API test shards used to spend 7 to 8 seconds installing the same Postgres client every run, so they baked it into a base image; since the repo is a pnpm workspace, tests used to install the whole workspace, and restricting installs to just the API package and its dependencies cut pnpm install from 44-73 seconds to 16-18 seconds. They also tested caching node_modules and found a cache hit was actually slower than a filtered install (28 seconds versus 7.5), because the lockfile changes often enough that the cache key keeps invalidating, so they dropped that cache entirely.
items.why: 这篇的价值在于全程带着实测数字，而不是一句「我们让 CI 更快了」。文中提到的情况（agent 让 PR 数量涨得比校验能力快）是任何在用 agent 批量写代码、又要保证质量关卡跟得上的团队，迟早会撞上的同一个瓶颈。
items.why_en: The value here is that it carries real measured numbers the whole way through, not just a claim of "we made CI faster." The situation it describes, agents making PR volume grow faster than validation capacity, is the same bottleneck any team leaning on agents for bulk code changes will eventually hit.

items.title: OpenAI 烧钱变少，账单反而涨了 43%
items.title_en: OpenAI's burn is falling while its bill grows 43%
items.author: TheNextWeb
items.summary:
《金融时报》拿到一份 OpenAI 今年 7 月为一笔算力交易准备的内部材料：2026 到 2030 年，公司预计的自由现金流缺口是 2780 亿美元，比 5 月给出的 3050 亿美元预测好了约 270 亿美元。同一份材料里，算力和基础设施这一项涨到了大约 8560 亿美元，比 2 月公开给投资人的 6000 亿美元目标高出约 43%（两个口径的定义可能不完全一致，部分差距或许来自统计范围）。同一份材料还给出 2030 年营收预期 3500 亿美元，对比今年大约 360 亿美元。

烧钱数字往下走、账单数字往上走能同时成立，原因是这些支出大半没有算在 OpenAI 自己的资产负债表上。OpenAI 没有投资级信用评级，融资大多靠别人背书：英伟达在谈判为 2500 亿美元的数据中心债务做担保，让放贷方按芯片厂商的信用定价；甲骨文在数据中心上的支出已经超过自己一个季度的营收，大头对应 OpenAI 的合同，但这笔资本支出记在甲骨文账上；SB Energy 用价值 55 亿美元的 OpenAI 认股权证换了一份 20 年租约，把一笔本该付现金的资本支出换成了用股权支付的经营支出。自由现金流量的是钱从一个具体主体账上流出多少，不是这个主体背上了多少义务，供应商、房东和合作方替你把账扛在自己身上时，这两个数字自然会分道扬镳。
items.summary_en:
The Financial Times obtained an internal OpenAI document prepared this past July for a compute deal: for 2026 through 2030, the company projects a negative free cash flow of $278 billion, an improvement of about $27 billion on the $305 billion it projected in May. The same document puts the compute and infrastructure line at roughly $856 billion, about 43% above the $600 billion target given publicly to investors in February (the two figures' definitions may not be fully identical, so part of the gap could be definitional). The same materials put 2030 revenue at $350 billion, against roughly $36 billion this year.

Burn falling while the bill rises can both be true because most of that spending doesn't sit on OpenAI's own balance sheet. OpenAI carries no investment-grade credit rating, so its financing mostly runs through other parties: Nvidia has been in talks to guarantee $250 billion of data-center debt, letting lenders price against the chipmaker's credit instead; Oracle is spending more on data centers than it earns in a quarter, much of it against OpenAI commitments, but that capex lands on Oracle's own books; SB Energy took $5.5 billion in OpenAI warrants to sign a 20-year lease, converting what would have been a cash capital expense into an equity-paid operating one. Free cash flow measures how much money leaves one specific entity, not how many obligations that entity has taken on, and when vendors, landlords, and partners carry the weight on their own books instead, the two numbers naturally diverge.
items.why: 两个数字放在一起读比单看哪一个都有用：一家公司完全可以一边告诉投资人烧钱在变少，一边把实际支出的大头转移给合作方来扛。评估任何一家扩张期公司的真实财务状况，先看清楚哪部分支出被移出了报表，再看烧钱数字。
items.why_en: Reading the two numbers together is more useful than looking at either alone: a company can perfectly well tell investors its burn is improving while shifting the bulk of its actual spending onto partners' books. When assessing any expansion-stage company's real finances, check what's been moved off the statement first, then look at the burn figure.

items.title: 九个技巧，把「技能」从提示词包装改成流程本身
items.title_en: Nine techniques that turn a "skill" from a wrapped prompt into the harness itself
items.author: 保罗·巴考斯 · AI Engineer 大会
items.author_en: Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable) · AI Engineer World's Fair
items.summary:
保罗·巴考斯写过 jQuery UI，当年把默认主题定成橙色，以为用的人会自己动手改颜色，结果没人改。这段经历成了他今天在 AI Engineer 大会讲「技能工程」的起点。他说人人吐槽的那种紫色渐变，原本只是某个 CSS 框架示例页的默认配色；现在 AI 生成的设计也有了自己的默认色，一种米黄色。他的判断是：禁用一种东西不会让输出变得原创，只会把模型推到潜在空间里下一个最近的簇。躲开一种俗气，换来的常常是另一种俗气，靶子一直在挪。

真正拉着模型往回走的是训练数据里最常见的那个中位数，几百字精心写的提示词拉不动它。所以他不再把「技能」当成裹了一层提示词的文件，而是当成整个运行环境的延伸。他举了几个具体做法：让两个子 agent 互相看不到对方的输出，一个当设计总监，一个跑死板的规则检查，因为一条线程自己给自己打分，几乎总会说做得不错；让模型先说出最想用的三个方案，再逼它把这三个全部扔掉，跳过那个安全的第一反应；写一个脚本，专门发给模型一串它猜不到的随机种子；把关键指令直接打在标准输出上而不是埋进大段提示词，模型照做的概率更高，代价是没法用提示词缓存；还有一种，是用钩子在写入发生之前直接拦下来，而不是等写完了再挑毛病。
items.summary_en:
Paul Bakaus wrote jQuery UI and shipped its default theme in orange, assuming people would swap in their own colors. Nobody did. That history opens his AI Engineer World's Fair talk on "skill engineering." The purple gradients everyone mocks, he points out, started as a CSS framework's own sample-page default; AI-generated design now has its own house shade, a kind of beige. His central claim: banning one thing doesn't make output original, it just pushes the model one cluster over in latent space. Dodge one flavor of slop and you usually land on another; the target keeps moving.

What actually holds the model in place is the median of its training data, and a few hundred carefully written words of prompt can't pull against that kind of gravity. So he stopped treating a "skill" as a prompt wrapped in a file and started treating it as an extension of the whole harness. Among the concrete moves he described: run two sub-agents blind to each other's output, one acting as design director and one running a deterministic linter, because a single thread grading its own work will almost always say it did fine; have the model name its top three preferred options, then force it to throw out all three, skipping the "safe" first instinct; write a script whose only job is handing the model a random seed it couldn't have guessed; print key instructions to standard output instead of burying them in prose, which models follow more reliably at the cost of losing prompt caching; and use hooks that block a write before it happens, instead of complaining about it afterward.
items.why: 这几招不是审美建议，是对 agent 运行流程本身动刀。用两个互相看不到结论的子 agent 做交叉核验，这个思路适用于任何要靠 AI 把关质量的场景，巴考斯只是把它明确用在了对付「AI 同款脸」上。
items.why_en: These aren't style tips, they're surgery on the agent's own operating pipeline. Running two sub-agents blind to each other's conclusions for cross-checking applies to any setting where AI is used to grade its own quality; Bakaus just points that method squarely at "AI sameface."

items.title: Astra 的客户名单，从法务扩到了设计和工程
items.title_en: Astra's customer list grows from law into design and engineering
items.author: OpenAI
items.summary:
上周五（09-18）OpenAI 发布 Astra for Law 时，把客户名字直接写进了公告，但跑分没有赢过对手。今天这套打法扩到了别的行业：OpenAI 一口气放出五条一两分钟的客户证言短片，每条对应一个客户，覆盖设计（Figma）、财务（Ramp）、企业知识管理（Notion）、法务与 IPO（Cooley）和内容管理（Box）。

Notion 的例子给了一个具体技术细节：工程师 Quinn Johnson 让 Astra 在 Codex 里自由排查一次缓存复用问题，Astra 发现了团队一直没注意到的模式：较早的消息会被按 agent 当前掌握的信息重新生成，悄悄改变了提示词历史，导致缓存复用失效。系统表面上还能正常工作，只是在悄悄变慢、变贵。Figma 的例子是设计生成：员工 John 让 Astra 设计一架私人飞机的飞行控制界面，Astra 先推演了用户群体、任务目标、飞行员与乘客的取舍，再通过 Figma 的 MCP 服务器接进真实设计系统，做出一版可用的原型。
items.summary_en:
Last Friday (09-18) when OpenAI launched Astra for Law, it named a customer directly in the announcement, but its benchmark scores didn't beat competitors. Today that same playbook expanded into other industries: OpenAI released five one-to-two-minute customer testimonial clips in one go, each built around a different customer, spanning design (Figma), finance (Ramp), enterprise knowledge work (Notion), law and IPOs (Cooley), and content management (Box).

The Notion example supplies one concrete technical detail: engineer Quinn Johnson let Astra freely investigate a cache-reuse issue inside Codex, and it found a pattern the team had missed: older messages were being regenerated using whatever the agent currently knew, subtly changing the prompt history and breaking cache reuse. The system still appeared to work while quietly getting slower and more expensive. Figma's example is about design generation: employee John had Astra design the flight-control interface for a personal aircraft; it reasoned through the target users, jobs to be done, and pilot-versus-passenger tradeoffs before connecting to a real design system via Figma's MCP Server to produce a usable prototype.
items.why: 这五条短片都是 OpenAI 自己出资拍的客户证言，不是独立评测，每条只讲一个正面案例，没有基准对照。上次法务那条的教训是客户名字写得响不代表跑分站得住；这次信息量比上次大一些，至少 Notion 的例子给了一个可以复核的具体技术细节（提示词历史被静默改写导致缓存失效），不只是一句「客户很满意」。
items.why_en: All five clips are customer testimonials OpenAI itself commissioned and paid for, not independent evaluations, and each tells one positive case with no benchmark comparison. The lesson from last time's law launch was that a loud customer name doesn't mean the benchmark holds up; this batch carries more substance, at least the Notion example gives one checkable technical detail (prompt history silently rewritten, breaking cache reuse), not just a line about a happy customer.
items.flag: 五条均为 OpenAI 自制客户证言，非独立评测，请按厂商自述对待
items.flag_en: All five clips are OpenAI's own customer testimonials, not independent evaluations; treat them as vendor-supplied accounts

items.title: TypeSafe 创始人：AI 不该学会聊天
items.title_en: TypeSafe's founder: AI shouldn't learn to chat
items.author: Diogo Almeida · TypeSafe · Latent Space
items.summary:
Diogo Almeida 早年在 OpenAI 参与过指令跟随模型的研发，后来创办 TypeSafe。Jev 上线引发关注没几天，他就上了 Latent Space，跟 swyx 聊了一期。他把 Jev 归为「系统一模型」：不生成文字，只在结构化 schema 上给出校准过的判断，面向代码与决策场景，看重的是每美元能换来多少智能，而非聊天体验。他谈到 RLHF 的失败模式，比如模式坍缩；也谈到当 AI 成为软件里的一个依赖项、不再是聊天窗口时，「拒绝回答」会变成完全不同的问题。他说 TypeSafe 不对齐公开跑分，因为跑分与真实场景差距太大；还说就算给十亿美元，也不会从头预训练模型，数据和任务选对了，比堆算力更重要。

Jev 上线以来，社区已复刻出至少六个版本；就在今天，Hacker News 首页又多了一个用 Qwen3.5 做底座的开源仿制品，叫 Kev，作者是 Jared Palmer。一个做法这么快被复刻，对「系统一模型」这条思路是否成立，也是一次社会验证。
items.summary_en:
Diogo Almeida previously worked on instruction-following models at OpenAI, then founded TypeSafe; a few days after Jev's launch drew attention, he joined swyx on Latent Space. He places Jev in a category he calls "System One Models": generates no text, only calibrated judgments over a structured schema, built for code and decision-making, optimized for intelligence per dollar rather than chat experience. He discussed RLHF failure modes like mode collapse, and how "refusing to answer" becomes an entirely different problem once AI is a dependency buried in software rather than a chat window. He says TypeSafe doesn't align to public benchmarks because the gap between benchmarks and real-world use is too large, and that even with a billion dollars, he wouldn't choose to pretrain a model from scratch, picking the right data and task matters more than piling on compute.

Since Jev launched, the community has produced at least six clones; today Hacker News's front page picked up yet another, an open clone built on Qwen3.5 called Kev, by Jared Palmer. How quickly a design gets copied is itself, in a way, a social test of whether the "System One Models" idea holds up.
items.why: 他这套说法目前只有他一人之言：TypeSafe 不发论文、不开放权重、也不跑公开榜单，所以「每美元能换多少智能」这类说法眼下没有外部核验的路径，只能当作创始人自述来读。
items.why_en: This is currently a one-sided account: TypeSafe publishes no paper, releases no weights, and doesn't run public benchmarks, so claims like "intelligence per dollar" have no outside way to check right now, read it as the founder's own account, not a verified result.
